entries.name: SimCLR
aliases: Simple framework for contrastive learning of visual representations
entries.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that jointly trains an encoder and a nonlinear projection head by contrasting two augmented views of each image against other images’ views in the same minibatch.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original 2020 SimCLR procedure, not a particular ResNet checkpoint, the general contrastive-learning category or SimCLR v2. It uses current-batch views and a shared gradient-trained encoder/projection head, rather than a queue of historical keys or a momentum target encoder. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 187 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive searches of both full checkouts found no discovery-checkout hits and nine unrelated main-environment substrings (Pygments and Sphinx locale/bundle text). Exact neighboring AIO definitions, synonyms and incident edges were inspected; task/network vocabulary does not make these algorithms equivalent.
entries.mechanism: For a minibatch of N≥2 images, independently augment each image twice to obtain 2N views. Encode each with the same f and nonlinear projection head g, giving z_i=g(f(v_i)). With nonzero projected vectors and temperature tau>0, set s_ik=z_i^T z_k/(||z_i|| ||z_k||). For anchor i and its paired view j, use loss ell(i,j)=−log[exp(s_ij/tau)/sum_(k≠i) exp(s_ik/tau)]. The denominator contains the positive j and the 2N−2 other-image views, while excluding i itself. Average over all 2N directed positive pairs and update both f and g by gradients. After pretraining, discard g and use the representation before projection from f for downstream learning.
entries.locator: Section 2.1, Figure 2 and Equation (1), PDF p. 2; Algorithm 1 and Sections 2.2–2.3, p. 3; Section 4.2, p. 6
limitations: The source’s image realization composes crop/resize/flip, color distortion and Gaussian blur. These choices determine the prediction task; an augmentation policy may remove information needed downstream.

Views from other images serve as negatives by construction, not by verified semantic dissimilarity. This does not establish class labels or guarantee that semantically related images never oppose one another.

The source uses global batch normalization to mitigate same-device information leakage between positive views. Distributed normalization and optimization choices matter to reproducing its experiments.

Projection normalization requires meaningful nonzero vectors and numerically stable loss evaluation. Batch size, temperature, architecture and training schedule affect the procedure’s empirical behavior.
Reported ImageNet and transfer comparisons are context-specific. No universal performance advantage, mutual-information explanation, trained checkpoint or reproduced benchmark is asserted.

entries.name: Momentum contrast
entries.definition: A contrastive representation-learning mechanism that maintains a queue of encoded negative keys and produces new keys with an encoder updated by an exponential moving average of the query encoder.
entries.identity_notes: This is original MoCo from the 2020 paper, with its image instance-discrimination realization. The momentum acts on encoder parameters, not on per-example memory-bank embeddings. It is distinct from MoCo v2/v3 and from large-batch end-to-end contrastive training. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 187 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive searches of both full checkouts found no discovery-checkout hits and nine unrelated main-environment substrings (Pygments and Sphinx locale/bundle text). Exact neighboring AIO definitions, synonyms and incident edges were inspected; task/network vocabulary does not make these algorithms equivalent.
entries.mechanism: Initialize key-encoder parameters from the query encoder and maintain a finite FIFO queue of K≥1 encoded keys. For each image draw two augmented views, form normalized query q and current positive key k+, and use loss −log[exp(q·k+/tau)/(exp(q·k+/tau)+sum_(k in queue)exp(q·k/tau))] with tau>0. Stop gradients through the key outputs and queue; update the query encoder from the minibatch loss. In paper Algorithm 1, next update key parameters as theta_k←m theta_k+(1−m)theta_q, m in [0,1), enqueue the keys already computed for this batch, and remove the oldest batch to maintain the queue. The queue decouples dictionary size from current minibatch size; the momentum encoder reduces changes between key representations created at different iterations.
entries.locator: Sections 3.1–3.3, Equations (1)–(2), Figure 2 and Algorithm 1, printed pp. 9730–9732 / PDF pp. 2–4
limitations: Queued keys were encoded at different parameter states. A slow update aims to improve consistency; it does not make historical keys identical to recomputed current-encoder outputs.
The image realization treats different images as negatives. This is instance discrimination, not verification that all negative pairs belong to different semantic classes.

The paper’s distributed ResNet implementation shuffles the key minibatch across GPUs and restores correspondence after encoding to reduce batch-normalization leakage. Other normalization choices need their own reproduction checks.

The displayed algorithm abstracts queue initialization and requires a valid finite dictionary. Temperature, queue length, momentum and augmentation are tuning choices; no single setting is universally optimal.
This record specifies the original paper’s update order and scope. It does not import later MoCo variants, claim independent samples, or reproduce benchmark training.

entries.name: Bootstrap Your Own Latent
entries.definition: A self-supervised image representation-learning procedure that trains an online predictor to match a stopped-gradient target projection from another augmented view, while updating the target encoder and projector by exponential moving averages.
entries.identity_notes: BYOL is the 2020 online/target learning procedure, not statistical bootstrap resampling or a particular trained network. Only the online branch has the prediction head. Its normalized regression objective has no explicit negative-pair term or historical key queue. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 187 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive searches of both full checkouts found no discovery-checkout hits and nine unrelated main-environment substrings (Pygments and Sphinx locale/bundle text). Exact neighboring AIO definitions, synonyms and incident edges were inspected; task/network vocabulary does not make these algorithms equivalent.
entries.mechanism: Generate two augmented views v and v′ of each image. The online branch computes p(v)=q_theta(g_theta(f_theta(v))), and the target branch computes z_xi(v′)=g_xi(f_xi(v′)). Normalize both nonzero vectors and minimize their squared distance, plus the reversed-view term p(v′) versus z_xi(v), averaged over the batch. Stop gradients at target projections and optimize only the online encoder, projector and predictor. After the optimizer step update the corresponding target encoder/projector parameters by xi←tau xi+(1−tau)theta with tau in [0,1] and a chosen decay schedule. The target branch has no predictor to update. After training retain the online encoder f_theta and discard the training heads and target branch for the stated downstream representation.
entries.locator: Section 3.1, Figure 2 and Equations (1)–(2), main PDF p. 4; Section 3.2, pp. 4–5; Section 5, pp. 7–8
limitations: The paper’s general same-architecture wording is qualified by its explicit online-only predictor in Figure 2 and the algorithm. Matching encoder/projector weights are averaged; a nonexistent target predictor is not required.

Absence of an explicit negative-pair term does not prove collapse impossible. The source’s conditional-variance explanation assumes an optimal predictor and simplified unnormalized, unsymmetrized dynamics; it is an intuition, not a general convergence theorem.
Batch normalization still couples examples. The batch-size ablation also accumulates gradients to control effective update size; it does not establish unconditional batch-size independence.

Augmentation, normalization, predictor design and target-decay schedule affect training. tau=1 freezes the target and tau=0 copies the online parameters; these endpoints do not by themselves reproduce the usual slow-target regime.
Vector normalization needs a defined nonzero-norm numerical treatment. No universal transfer benefit, benchmark reproduction or model checkpoint is asserted.

entries.name: DINO self-distillation
entries.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that matches cross-view student probabilities to centered and sharpened probabilities from a momentum teacher, without a separate prediction head or explicit negative-pair objective.
entries.identity_notes: This is Caron et al.’s 2021 DINO self-distillation method, supporting both vision-transformer and convolutional backbones. It is not the later DINO object detector, DINOv2/v3, or a particular checkpoint. The bare acronym is not asserted as an unqualified alias. Its same-architecture student/teacher branches differ from BYOL’s online-only predictor and normalized vector regression. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 187 prior native IDs/names/aliases. Ignored-inclusive searches of both full checkouts found no discovery-checkout hits and nine unrelated main-environment substrings (Pygments and Sphinx locale/bundle text). Exact neighboring AIO definitions, synonyms and incident edges were inspected; task/network vocabulary does not make these algorithms equivalent.
entries.mechanism: Initialize teacher parameters from the student and a center c=0. Generate two global crops and optional local crops from each image; the teacher sees the global crops and the student sees all crops. For raw K-dimensional outputs g, use P_s(v)=softmax(g_s(v)/tau_s) and P_t(v)=softmax((g_t(v)−c)/tau_t), with positive temperatures and a sharpened teacher distribution. Average cross-entropy −sum_i P_t(v)_i log P_s(v′)_i over teacher global crops and student crops of the same image, excluding the identical view, and average over images in the minibatch. Stop gradients through P_t, update student parameters by the loss, and update teacher parameters by theta_t←lambda theta_t+(1−lambda)theta_s, with lambda in [0,1]. Update c by an exponential moving average with center momentum in [0,1) of the raw teacher outputs over all global views in the distributed batch for use on subsequent batches. Both branches share backbone and projection-head architecture; downstream features are taken from the backbone before the head.
entries.locator: Sections 3.1–3.2, Algorithm 1, Equations (1)–(4), printed pp. 9652–9654 / PDF pp. 3–5; Section 5, printed p. 9657 / PDF p. 8
limitations: The centering prose on printed p. 9653 says to add c, whereas Algorithm 1 subtracts the running center. The pinned author implementation also subtracts it; this record follows the algorithm and implementation and preserves the discrepancy.
The teacher is updated from the student, not supplied as an independently trained larger model. Its output coordinates are learned representation probabilities, not verified semantic class labels.
Centering and sharpening are empirical collapse-control choices, not a proof that all initializations, temperatures, momentum schedules or datasets avoid collapsed representations.
A larger number of local crops changes the cross-view objective. The two-view pseudocode is a specialization; losses exclude the teacher/student pair from the identical crop.

The pinned implementation uses zero center initialization, distributed raw-output averaging and matched initial student/teacher weights. Its specific default temperature schedule differs from the paper’s reported experimental schedule; this record does not equate all defaults.
No DINO detector mechanism, later DINO variant, segmentation accuracy claim, trained checkpoint or executed benchmark is asserted.

mapping_assessment: Read twelve exact CLASS nodes and their synonyms/incident edges, enumerated in source_analysis.aio_mapping_inspection. All four algorithms have related mappings to the SelfsupervisedLearning task. SimCLR and MoCo also relate to ContrastiveLearning, exported beneath DeepNeuralNetwork. LLM terms have wrong scope and RandomContrastLayer means pixel preprocessing. No AIO pin or generated record changed.

moco2020.notes: Original MoCo 2020: queue plus momentum encoder, general pretext mechanism with instance-discrimination realization. One current positive key plus K queued negative keys; normalized ResNet last-FC embeddings. InfoNCE denominator includes positive. Initialize key encoder from query, detach keys, no key backprop. Algorithm1: update query by gradients, then EMA key parameters, then enqueue already-computed current keys/dequeue oldest batch. EMA parameters differ from per-sample memory-bank EMA. Shuffle key minibatch across GPUs and unshuffle features to prevent paired BN leakage. Do not conflate MoCo v2/v3. Published pages9729–9738.
